context: Exact room messages from a real, isolated Abralo workspace. Alex is the fictional operator account used for this demonstration. All three employees ran Codex. Local project paths are replaced with <demo-project>. The launch operator supplied the brief and later integrated and polished the website.

messages.author: Alex
messages.text: @Simulation engineer build a little city whose traffic really reacts when someone closes a bridge. Follow BRIEF.md for the model, map and accessibility contracts. Hand the engine to Cartographer, then hand the finished scene to Reviewer. Make it something people want to play with, and keep the work and findings in this room.

messages.author: Simulation engineer
messages.text:
I’ll read BRIEF.md, implement the traffic engine within my assigned files, and check bridge closure behavior before handing it to Cartographer.


The engine now routes cars across the road graph, keeps spacing within each lane, and lets cars already on a closed bridge finish crossing. I’m checking rerouting, queue recovery, deterministic stepping and reset behavior.


The checks passed: closed bridges admitted no new cars, lane gaps held, and queued cars recovered after reopening. Over 60 simulated seconds, busy demand admitted 181 trips versus 65 in calm mode. The API documentation is ready for the map handoff.


Implemented and documented the traffic engine. Local checks passed for deterministic stepping, bridge closures, rerouting, following gaps, bounded queues and recovery after reopening.

Handed the engine to Cartographer in this room. The scene and browser verification remain pending.

messages.author: Simulation engineer
messages.text: I’m implementing the engine contract in BRIEF.md: seeded traffic, fixed simulation steps, road following gaps, junction queues and bridge-aware routing. I’ll document the API and run local behavior checks before the map handoff.

messages.author: Simulation engineer
messages.text: @Cartographer The engine is ready in city-engine.mjs, with the contract and model details in API.md. Please implement city-view.mjs and preview.html within the BRIEF.md file boundaries, then continue its prescribed handoff. Positions already include a 5-unit right-hand lane offset; angle is canvas heading in radians. Directed edges expose length and bridge/closed flags; deduplicate reverse pairs when drawing roads. Node IDs are n<row>-<column>. Inline Node assertions passed for deterministic frame chunking, reset, validation, clamp, snapshot isolation, demand, closure entry prevention, rerouting, lane gaps, bounded/finite state, conservation and reopening recovery; node --check also passed. All-closed traffic queued safely (26/26 active waiting in the checked run), and arrivals resumed after reopening. package.json provides npm test for the later tests/*.mjs suite. No browser or performance verification has been claimed.

messages.author: Cartographer
messages.text:
I’ll read the brief and engine contract, build the city scene and controls, then hand the finished files to Reviewer in this thread.


The scene and controls are implemented: roofed terraces, a market, clock court, riverside details, visible traffic and closure barriers. I’m checking the renderer contract and mobile hit targets before the review handoff.


Implemented the architectural map and accessible preview controls in `city-view.mjs` and `preview.html`, then handed them to Reviewer.

Syntax and mock-context checks passed, including mobile bridge targets and deterministic drawing. Browser, accessibility and performance verification remain pending.

messages.author: Cartographer
messages.text: I’m building the warm architectural map and standalone controls in city-view.mjs and preview.html. The renderer will use the engine’s exact roads and car positions, with generous bridge targets and keyboard-accessible controls. I’ll hand the files and actual verification results to Reviewer here.

messages.author: Cartographer
messages.text: @Reviewer The scene is ready in city-view.mjs and preview.html. Please add the prescribed tests/ integration suite and REVIEW.md, and review renderer correctness within your BRIEF.md ownership. The map draws deduplicated engine roads, existing lane-offset car positions, roofed terraces, a market, clock court, gardens and river details. Closures add barriers and X markers; bridge hit targets use the same projection with a 44px minimum. The host provides bridge buttons, pause, demand, reset, live engine statistics, status announcements and reduced-motion initial pause. Only my two assigned files changed. node --check passed for the renderer and extracted preview module. Inline Node recording-context assertions passed for deterministic finite drawing, state restoration, snapshot immutability and bridge targets at 320/720/1440 widths. These were mock-context checks; browser appearance, real interactions, accessibility and performance remain unverified for the operator’s final pass.

messages.author: Reviewer
messages.text:
I’ll read the brief, engine and renderer, then add and run the integration suite and record findings in REVIEW.md.


The engine and renderer match the documented API on inspection. I’m adding checks for tick-by-tick closure behavior, road geometry, counters, and preview control wiring. Browser appearance and real accessibility testing remain part of the operator’s final pass.


The suite is running. It checks recovery through a single reopened bridge, shortest routes against an independent path calculation, and renderer geometry with a recording canvas context. It also exercises the preview’s controls and pause behavior in a mocked host.


All 14 tests passed; no defects surfaced in the checked behavior. I’m recording the results and limits in REVIEW.md. The suite does not establish browser appearance, screen-reader usability, or frame performance.


Added the integration suite and REVIEW.md. All 14 tests passed; no defects found in the checked cases. Implementation unchanged.

Results reported in this room. Real browser visuals, accessibility and performance remain unverified; exact coverage and limits are documented in the attached review.

messages.author: Simulation engineer
messages.text:
I’ll read Cartographer’s handoff and check the local files so I can report what’s complete and what remains unverified.


The engine and city scene are implemented, including bridge-aware routing, visible queues, closure barriers, and controls for bridges, demand, pause and reset.

Engine behavior checks passed. Cartographer reports passing syntax and mock-context checks, including mobile hit targets and deterministic drawing.

Browser appearance, real interactions, accessibility and performance remain unverified. The existing handoff is recorded in this room; I haven’t repeated it.

messages.author: Reviewer
messages.text: I’m reviewing the engine/view contracts and adding tests/integration.mjs plus REVIEW.md. I’ll check routing and recovery, determinism, invariants and renderer integration, and report exact results and remaining browser limits here.

messages.author: Reviewer
messages.text: Review complete. Added tests/integration.mjs and REVIEW.md only. `node --test tests/integration.mjs` passed 14/14 tests on Node v24.16.0 (23.93s), covering seed/reset/chunking, shortest routing, individual and all-bridge closures/recovery, finite bounded state, counters, validation, renderer geometry/state and mocked preview controls. No defects found in the checked cases; implementation unchanged. REVIEW.md records exact coverage and limits. Real browser appearance, keyboard/touch and screen-reader behavior, DPR rendering and frame performance remain unverified for the operator’s final pass. Both files are attached to the review reply.

messages.author: Cartographer
messages.text:
I’ll read Reviewer’s findings and incorporate the verified results into the handoff.


The city scene and controls are complete. Reviewer reports all 14 integration tests passed, with no defects found in the checked cases.

[Review findings](/api/attachments/7d4078a6-20e4-483c-b8ec-ece33d6a9adb) cover routing, closure recovery, renderer geometry and mocked controls. Real browser visuals, accessibility and frame performance remain for the operator’s final pass.

messages.author: Alex
messages.text: The integrated website now passes Chromium checks at 320, 390, 768 and 1440 pixels: moving traffic, keyboard and touch bridge controls, rush hour, deterministic reset, pause, offscreen suspension, reduced motion and failure fallback. I added an optional static-map cache to the renderer and reran the independent suite: all 14 tests passed. The public notebook will retain the original brief, review and exact room messages. This is a small traffic toy; the review limits still apply. The website integration and visual polish were performed by the launch operator.
